system.description: Human NEMO zinc-finger domain with deprotonated coordinating cysteines and one zinc ion

publication.citation: Godwin R, Gmeiner W, Salsbury FR Jr. Importance of long-time simulations for rare event sampling in zinc finger proteins. J Biomol Struct Dyn. 2016;34(1):125-134.

starting_structure_reference.description: Solution structure of human NEMO zinc finger

time_axis.basis: Matching archived NAMD inputs declare timestep 2.0 fs and dcdfreq 100. The DCD was rewritten by a DCD plugin and does not retain an independently interpretable physical interval.
time_axis.caveat: The publication reports separately selected analysis save rates. This tutorial value describes the archived raw sample, not every trajectory analyzed in the paper.

derivation.policy: contiguous prefix; source read without modification

rights_note: The group-generated PSF and 1,000-frame trajectory subset are released under CC BY 4.0 as specified in the repository's LICENSE-DATA.md. The starting coordinates derive from PDB 2JVX and retain that source's provenance; the repository does not claim the underlying PDB record as original Salsbury-group data.
limitations: The subset is intentionally short and begins at source frame zero.
It is suitable for learning the software and checking execution, not for estimating converged populations, kinetics, free energies, or zinc-binding mechanisms.
A technically complete workflow does not make the tutorial subset scientifically adequate.
The cited publication itself explains why long simulations are needed to observe rare zinc-finger conformations.
